evidence.claim: In a closed market, a lender can execute a withdrawal before all requests are added to the batch; later small withdrawals dilute the batch rate via rounding, so an earlier withdrawer takes more than their pro-rata share and the last withdrawer's executeWithdrawal reverts (insufficient normalizedUnclaimedWithdrawals).
evidence.support_reason: In a closed market, _executeWithdrawal skips the expiry check (line 239: `if (expiry >= block.timestamp && !state.isClosed)`), so a lender can execute against a partially-filled batch. newTotalWithdrawn = mulDiv(batch.normalizedAmountPaid, status.scaledAmount, batch.scaledTotalAmount) (line 248) is computed against the batch's current scaledTotalAmount; later queueWithdrawal calls (line 114) increase batch.scaledTotalAmount, lowering the per-scaled-token rate for subsequent executions. Earlier executions are not clawed back, so the sum of payouts can exceed the final batch.normalizedAmountPaid, and the last executor's normalizedAmountWithdrawn can exceed remaining state.normalizedUnclaimedWithdrawals (line 258), reverting on underflow.
preconditions: Market is closed (borrower calls closeMarket) while a withdrawal batch is pending and not fully paid
Multiple lenders queue withdrawals into the same batch after the first execution
Rounding down of small scaled amounts reduces the batch's effective rate
